name: Laddering
description:
Laddering is an interviewing technique that moves between concrete attributes and deeper reasons, consequences or values by repeatedly asking participants why something matters. The researcher begins with a specific preference, feature or behaviour and progressively explores its significance.

The resulting chains can help designers understand connections between product characteristics, experiences and personal values.
whenToUse: Use laddering when you need to understand why particular features, choices or experiences matter to people rather than simply knowing which option they prefer.
steps: Begin with a concrete choice, attribute or experience.
Ask the participant why it is important.
Ask what consequence follows from that answer.
Continue asking why that consequence matters.
Record the chain from concrete attribute toward broader value.
lookOutFor: Repeatedly asking *'why?'* can become uncomfortable or interrogative. Vary the phrasing and respect participants' boundaries.
Do not assume every preference has a single deep underlying value.
The interviewer's expectations can influence where a ladder appears to end.

resources.citation: Reynolds, T. J. & Gutman, J. (1988). “Laddering Theory, Method, Analysis, and Interpretation.” *Journal of Advertising Research*, 28(1), 11–31.
